input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 (second instance, p0046) binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete ("any product or service that competes with Vendor"), in any territory, for the term plus 24 months. That is walk-away territory on both counts (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined competing scope) and fails every fallback element: no named product, post-term application, 24 months, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and convert the prohibition into an express permission, which removes the restriction and aligns 12.4 with 12.3. The separate no-hire restriction in the first Section 12.4 (p0045) is addressed under the no-hire rule, not here.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Convert Section 12.4's term-plus-24-month non-compete into an express permission
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or services we may develop, buy, or sell, so we have removed the term-plus-24-month non-compete in Section 12.4, which also contradicted Section 12.3's confirmation that we gave no non-compete commitment. If you need protection, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only and no longer than 12 months, carving out our internal development and acquisitions.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire
ops.newText: Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire
